proposals.name: Measured-Headroom Racing (MHR): probe-and-eliminate prescription over the mechanism × source grid
proposals.core_criterion: Prescribe data by MEASURED MARGINAL RETURN, not predicted need: the criterion is the causally measured ceiling of ΔSR per unit budget that a (mechanism, data-source) pair can deliver on its own pre-registered target slice, net of measured retention loss. Formally, each arm a=(m,s) — mechanism m ∈ {tall-grasp (h>0.21m handled/lidded categories), far-approach (|along-counter|>0.65), hard-style (49/43/42/21/22), never-succeed config list (28% of repeated configs)} crossed with source s ∈ {expert-loop, MimicGen-from-source, human teleop, later G1} — is scored by L̂_{m,s}, the paired-eval lift of a small probe fine-tune, decomposed logit-additively as L_{m,s} ≈ α_m (headroom of the mechanism) + β_s (expressiveness of the source for that mechanism's skill). Demo-type is NOT a free axis: the mechanism dissociation (far ⇒ never-touch ⇒ approach-emphasis demos; tall ⇒ touch-then-fumble ⇒ grasp-securing demos) pins demo-type to m, collapsing the arm space to ~4×3. The flat dose-response (r=0.06) and the saturation result (610 demos → 0.14 tall SR, worse than 200 → 0.21) dictate the return model: ΔSR_a(b) = L_a·(1−e^{−b/τ}) with τ ≈ 100–200 demos, so nearly all uncertainty is in the ceiling L_a, one small probe reveals ≈ all of an arm's information, and the problem is fixed-budget ARM IDENTIFICATION (which (m,s) pairs clear a bar), not dose optimization. This is why the bandit is a successive-elimination race, and why an arm with maximal P(fail) but L̂≈0 (the tall cliff under policy-collected data — generation ceiling) is eliminated where P(fail) targeting would pour budget into it.
proposals.scoring_rule: Score per arm: U_a = w_m · L̂_{m,s} / c_s − λ·max(0, −Δ̂_ret,a), with w_m = population prevalence of the target slice (far band = 26% of episodes; tall categories and hard styles computed from pooled_episodes.csv; never-succeed list = 28% of repeated configs), c_s = per-demo cost (expert-loop ≈ 1, MimicGen ≈ 2–3×, human ≈ 20×), Δ̂_ret = paired lift on the fixed retention slice, λ large enough that retention acts as a soft constraint (λ ≈ 2·w_m so a −5pp retention hit cancels a +10pp target win). L̂_{m,s} is estimated by causal probe (below), then SHRUNK across the grid via pooled config-clustered logistic regression of paired per-config outcome differences on mechanism and source main effects (Δlogit_{g,a} = α_{m(a)} + β_{s(a)} + small γ): justified because the report shows factors are log-odds additive with zero held-out interaction R² (0.1187→0.1182), so information transfers across arms sharing an axis or a source. Decision rule (successive elimination, not Thompson): ELIMINATE arm a if UCB95(L_a) < Δ* = 8pp on its target slice OR LCB90(Δ_ret,a) < −3pp; ADVANCE if LCB90(L_a) ≥ Δ*; otherwise re-probe once. Δ* = 8pp is the smallest effect the 78%-stochasticity floor lets a 300-episode paired eval resolve (see estimation), i.e., the threshold-of-caring is set by the noise floor, not by ambition. Thompson sampling is mismatched three ways: pulls are expensive and few (a pull = generate + LoRA + 300-ep eval), returns saturate at the first pull (τ small ⇒ repeated pulls of a winner buy nothing, so cumulative-regret machinery has no purchase), and the end decision is threshold identification with an audit trail — frequentist confidence bounds with pre-registered Δ* give winner's-curse-proof error control that a posterior-sampling trace does not.
proposals.estimation: One probe = (i) generate b₀ = 150 arm demos with the arm's demo-type — fixed-context generation (policy_analysis/fixed_context.py, high seeds ≥100000) for object-axis arms so per-object signal isn't swamped by ±12pp env noise; standard variation for region arms; MimicGen from source demos and human teleop are the sources that escape the policy-success bias of the pool; (ii) mix 50/50 with 150 base-coverage demos (the empirically validated coverage-preserving ratio: core lost −0.1pp on non-targeted vs coverage-arm −8.9pp); (iii) LoRA fine-tune from ONE frozen base checkpoint for the whole campaign; (iv) evaluate on pre-registered PAIRED seed lists — 150 distinct target-slice configs + 150 distinct retention configs, 1 rollout per config, identical seed lists for every arm and the baseline. Statistics: paired difference-in-proportions with config-level clustered SEs — mandatory, since the report shows episode-level tests are anticonservative (side test p=0.0026 episode-level vs p≈0.32 config-level). Pairing removes the measured (11.9%) + config-idiosyncratic (10.3%) variance shares; the irreducible 78% rollout stochasticity sets the floor: SE(Δ̂) ≈ sqrt(2·p(1−p)·0.78/n_c) ≈ 4.9pp at p≈0.4, n_c=150 → 80% power only for L ≳ 10–12pp; below n_c ≈ 120 every arm is indistinguishable (SE > 5.5pp) — this floor is what caps the round at ~6 arms and forbids cell-level (per-category) prescription outright, since per-cell n would need ~300 configs per cell. Winner's curse guard: with k=6 arms at SE 4.9pp, E[max] of pure noise ≈ +6pp — the same order as true effects — so round-1 point estimates are never reported or allocated on; survivors are REPLICATED in round 2 with a second LoRA seed and 300 fresh target configs (SE ≈ 3.5pp incl. seed variance), and only round-2 numbers feed allocation. Empirical-Bayes shrinkage through the α_m+β_s model further deflates outliers. Cost per probe ≈ 150 gen demos + 1 LoRA + 300 eval episodes ≈ 1 day on the H100 box; round 1 total ≈ 900 demos + 1,800 episodes.
proposals.allocation: Fixed-budget, three-round race. ROUND 1 (probe): 6 arms chosen as a fractional design over the 4×3 grid — every mechanism and every source appears ≥2× — and the expert-loop row is seeded warm from prior arms (we already know α_tall+β_expert ≈ 0 from the 610-demo saturation arm and α_far+β_expert ≈ 0 from the untouched rim penalty, so expert-loop gets ONE control arm, not four). Concretely: (tall, MimicGen), (tall, human), (far, MimicGen), (far, human-approach), (hard-style, MimicGen), (never-succeed-list, expert-loop control). Apply elimination rule. ROUND 2 (confirm): survivors (expect 2–3) re-run with 2nd LoRA seed + fresh 300-config target eval. ROUND 3 (commit): solve max Σ_a w_m·L_a·(1−e^{−b_a/τ̂}) s.t. Σ c_s·b_a ≤ B, base-mixture fraction ≥ 50%, predicted retention ≥ −2pp. With saturating returns this reduces to water-filling: fund confirmed arms in descending w_m·L̂_a/c_s at b* ≈ 2τ̂ ≈ 300 demos each until B (600-demo scale) is exhausted — and NEVER above ~300/arm, because the saturation arm proved dose beyond τ is not just wasted but harmful (610 → 0.299 vs 200 → 0.371 overall). Human-teleop arms are funded only where a cheaper source showed L̂≈0 on a high-headroom mechanism (tall: baseline SR 0.09, headroom ≈ 40pp) — that is the decision-theoretic formalization of the generation-ceiling escalation ladder. The retention constraint is structural, not scored: the ≥50% base fraction rides in every fine-tune, and the single fixed 300-config retention seed list is shared across the entire campaign so retention deltas are paired and precise.
proposals.validation: Final confirmatory 4-way, all paired on identical seed lists, config-clustered inference, pre-registered before the run: (A) MHR-prescribed mixture, (B) equal-budget RANDOM-selection mixture from the same sources — the non-negotiable control, since random captured ~80% of the targeted lift (+8.9 vs +11.0pp) and any claim must beat it, not the baseline; (C) equal-budget P(fail)-core incumbent (the old criterion); (D) frozen base. Three eval slices: 300 target-region configs, 300 retention configs, and ~100 configs sampled from the enumerated never-succeed list (re-verified under the frozen base first). Pre-registered success pattern: A−B ≥ +5pp on target (clustered p<0.05); A retention ≥ −2pp; and A produces successes on ≥5% of never-succeed configs where the expert-loop control produced none — that last cell is the qualitative kill-shot, because a fixed-pool-resistant config succeeding under new-source data is direct evidence for the generation-ceiling thesis. Falsification patterns, each with a designated interpretation: (i) all sources including human show L̂≈0 on tall → the weakness is not data-addressable at this model scale (embodiment/architecture), the criterion correctly returns "prescribe nothing here," and the paper pivots to that finding; (ii) B ≈ A on target → region-targeting adds nothing beyond generic fine-tuning at 200–600-demo budgets and the honest headline is coverage-preserving generic data; (iii) target lift only at the cost of retention despite 50% base → the constraint set is infeasible at this budget; report the lift-retention frontier rather than a point.
proposals.failure_modes: (1) False elimination by probe noise: at SE 4.9pp a true L=10pp arm is missed ~30% of the time if eliminated on point estimates — hence elimination only on UCB95 < Δ*, and eliminated arms stay alive inside the shared α_m+β_s model, auto-reinstated if a sibling probe raises α_m. (2) Dead arm ≠ dead data: L̂≈0 can mean the LoRA/LR/epoch recipe under-fit the new demos, not that the source lacks the skill; diagnostic before believing any zero — training loss on the probe demos (fits-but-no-lift = expressiveness verdict stands; doesn't-fit = optimization problem, retune first; the G1 SREE case proves curation/fit issues masquerade as data failures). (3) Base-checkpoint non-stationarity: L is conditional on the frozen base; committing round-3 data shifts the policy and invalidates cached L̂ — never reuse ceilings across bases, re-probe after any commit. (4) τ misspecification: the flat dose-response was measured on the biased pool; a genuinely new source could have threshold-at-higher-dose returns; run one dose-response satellite on the best surviving arm at b ∈ {75,150,300} — if L̂(300) ≫ L̂(150), the saturating prior is wrong and water-filling under-funds winners. (5) Goodhart on enriched slices: target-slice lifts overstate population impact; all allocation and reporting uses population-weighted w_m·ΔSR, and the untouched axes are monitored for the uniform-lift illusion (core's rim "gain" +11.2pp exactly equaled its center gain — zero differential). (6) Stale hard-config list: the 28% never-succeed set was defined on past checkpoints; re-verify a 50-config subsample under the frozen base before using it as an eval slice. (7) Optimistic pairing gain: the 22% variance reduction from pairing is an estimate; recompute all SEs each round by bootstrap over configs rather than trusting the formula.
proposals.why_beats_pfail_and_influence: P(fail) targeting and gradient influence are both zero-cost PROXIES for the same latent quantity — the causal ΔSR from adding specific data — and both failed by proxy bias in ways the verified record now quantifies. P(fail) ranks cells by need, not treatability: it maximally scores the tall cliff, where the measured return of policy-collected data is ≈0 even at 610 demos, because the pool is policy-success-biased and cannot contain the missing skill (generation ceiling) — and it is source-blind, so it cannot even pose the question that matters now, namely whether the SAME axis has L>0 under MimicGen or human data. Influence is a first-order Taylor estimate of L that works only when the loss gradient encodes the target (the project's own validated gating principle: whitening 0.605→0.677, RC-LESS-v2 ≈ core), and it optimized selection while ignoring retention — which the arm results proved is the binding constraint (value-influence: −9.4pp non-targeted). MHR replaces the proxy with the measurement: L is estimated by causal probe fine-tunes, made affordable by two verified structural facts that weren't available when the proxies were chosen — log-odds additivity lets ~6 probes inform the whole mechanism×source grid instead of probing every cell, and fast-saturating returns mean one 150-demo dose reveals essentially an arm's entire value, so direct measurement costs about one H100-day per arm. Retention enters as a hard structural constraint (50% base mixture + paired retention slice), not a hoped-for side effect. And the criterion's α_m+β_s decomposition converts the prior "failures" into the framework's warm start and its scientific payload: expert-loop rows with L≈0 next to human/MimicGen rows with L>0 on the same mechanism IS the generation-ceiling claim, measured — something neither P(fail) nor influence could ever exhibit, because neither varies the data source.

proposals.name: Treatable Failure Mass (TFM) prescription — mechanism-matched marginal treatment effects
proposals.core_criterion: Prescribe data not where the policy fails, but where a specific demo TYPE is measured to treat the CAUSE of a specific failure MECHANISM. The unit of prescription is a tuple (mechanism m, demo type d, source s, dose n, context diversity), and the decision quantity is treatable failure mass: TFM(m,d,s) = w_m x tau(d,s -> m), where w_m is the failure mass attributable to mechanism m on the target eval distribution and tau is the causal transfer coefficient of demo type d from source s onto mechanism-m probe cells, measured by micro fine-tune ablations NET of a same-size generic-data control, subject to a hard retention constraint on non-targeted performance. The verified landscape licenses this: failure mechanisms dissociate cleanly (far-from-sink = never-touch approach failure; tall>0.212m = touch-then-fumble grasp gate, -23.6pp; hard styles = perceptual difficulty hurting grasp AND post-grasp AND speed; handled/lidded categories = affordance residual beyond height), the factors are log-odds ADDITIVE with zero interaction R², so each mechanism is an independent targeting axis with its own matched treatment — and the arm results prove that failure probability alone is the wrong criterion because the highest-P(fail) cells (tall, rim) absorbed up to 610 pool demos with zero cell-level movement. The criterion's second clause is the escalation rule: when tau is measured ~0 for a source (as the saturation arm already measured for pool->tall), buy from the next source up the ladder (MimicGen -> human teleop -> G1), never more dose from the same source.
proposals.scoring_rule: Fixed mechanism-treatment pairing (pre-registered from the confirmed factor analysis, NOT selected from a table — this kills winner's curse at the design level): M1 approach (along-counter distance from sink, FE slope -0.35, +7.8pp never-touched) <- far-placement full-reach demos; M2 grasp-securing (h>0.212m gate, -23.6pp, touch-then-fumble, graspable-body tall) <- tall-object grasp demos from a NON-policy source (tau(pool->M2)~0 is already measured: 610 demos -> tall SR 0.14 vs core 0.21, cliff unmoved); M3 perceptual (style true SD 0.08 SR, best-worst 0.31, split-half r=0.69) <- the SAME manipulation demos replicated across hard styles 49/43/42/21/22 (mechanism is visual, not motor, so policy-source demos re-collected/replayed under hard styles are admissible); M4 affordance residual (kettle -0.49, blender_jug -0.37, saucepan_lid -0.33; handle-topped tall are never-touch) <- per-category MimicGen expansions from 1-3 human source demos each. Excluded by mechanism-share: place-stage data (treats ~2% of failures), layout (null), width (null). Portfolio value V = sum_m w_m * tau_m(n_m, s_m), maximized over doses subject to sum n_m + n_cov = B (200-600) and retention R(portfolio) >= -2pp. tau_m(n) is concave with a measured knee (dose-response r=0.06 within-mechanism and the 610-demo saturation justify a hard per-mechanism cap ~150 demos from any one source). Allocate to (m,d,s) only if the lower 80% CI bound of w_m * tau_shrunk exceeds a floor of +1pp overall-SR-equivalent; otherwise escalate source or return the budget to coverage. w_m = P(config in m's causal band on eval distribution) x band penalty (computable today from factor_analysis/pooled_episodes.csv: e.g. M1 ~ 0.26 x 18.3pp ~ 4.8pp of absolute SR), cross-checked against the mechanism classification of the enumerable 28% never-succeed configs via their modal failure phase (0.926 cross-run repeatability makes this classification reliable).
proposals.estimation: (a) w_m from existing pooled data (7,112 episodes) at zero new cost: band membership x run-adjusted penalty, config-clustered CIs (the report's §9 warning is binding: episode-level permutation gave p=0.0026 where config-level gives p~0.32 — every test clusters on config signature). Second estimate: classify each of the ~330 never-succeed repeated configs into a mechanism by modal failure phase + factor band; configs matching no band go to a residual bucket (this also bounds how much of the 10.3% config-idiosyncratic variance the taxonomy misses). (b) tau via mechanism probe micro-arms, one week of H100: for each of the 4 pairings, generate N=120 demos of type d (M1: MimicGen replays at large along-counter placements, approach segment re-planned; M2: MimicGen from 3-5 human source demos of tall grasps — first non-policy rung; M3: fixed-context style sweep re-collection of existing successful behaviors under the 5 hardest styles; M4: MimicGen per hard category), LoRA fine-tune with the identical recipe as prior arms, plus ONE random/generic 120-demo control arm. (c) Every fine-tune is evaluated on a single shared FACTORIAL probe eval (~300 eps, paired seeds across all arms): 4 fixed-context mechanism bands (~50 eps each, seeded with never-succeed configs from that band, pinned layout/style/robot-base per fixed_context.py, interior placement except M1's far band) + ~100-ep standard-distribution retention slice. This yields a full tau matrix tau(d -> m') for every d — the diagonality of that matrix IS the verification that a demo type treats its mechanism (the lens's transfer check): tau_hat(d->m) = [SR_d(band_m) - SR_random(band_m)], config-clustered SE, EB-shrunk toward 0 with prior variance set by the cross-cell spread. Differencing against the random control removes the generic-fine-tuning lift that contaminated prior arms (random captured ~80% of core's region lift; core-random only +2pp ns). Power: probe bands concentrate episodes where baseline SR is 0.09-0.33, so headroom is large; at 50 clustered eps/band the MDE is ~12-15pp — adequate for the tau we care about (a treatment that moves a band <10pp is below the allocation floor anyway). Winner's curse safeguards: pairings pre-registered, only 4 confirmatory taus estimated (no selection over a menu), and no dose/source chosen from the same eval that certifies it (two-stage design below). R(d) is read off each arm's retention slice directly (the harness already produces it: core -0.1 vs coverage -8.9, influence -4.4, value -9.4).
proposals.allocation: Two-tier budget for B=600 (scale down proportionally for 200). Tier 1, coverage floor: ~200 demos (1/3) of broad-distribution data, PLUS the constraint that every targeted demo is generated with interior placement variation (shrink region to ~(0.15,0.20), not a pinned point) and >=3 styles — this is the retention constraint made structural, since coverage preservation was the verified real edge of the best arm and the concentrated arms (value/coverage) lost 9pp collateral. Tier 2, ~400 demos allocated across mechanisms by greedy water-filling on shrunken marginal value w_m * tau_m, capped at 150/mechanism/source (saturation-justified), with the source-escalation rule: if the stage-1 probe gives tau(s->m) CI overlapping 0, do NOT buy more from s — escalate (pool -> MimicGen -> human teleop -> G1) and re-probe at 60 demos before committing. Given current measurements the expected initial portfolio is roughly: M2 tall-MimicGen 150 (largest per-band headroom, SR 0.09 baseline, and the mechanism where the generation ceiling is proven so the escalation test is most informative), M1 far-placement 100, M4 affordance MimicGen 100 across the 4-6 hardest categories (1 human source demo each -> MimicGen multiplies; no dose-response means breadth-across-categories beats depth-per-category), M3 style replication 50 (cheapest per demo; behaviors already exist, only context changes), residual/unclassified never-succeed configs get NO targeted budget (they are coverage's job) until seed-replay metadata extraction assigns them a mechanism. If any tau comes back ~0 at the top source available in sim, that budget returns to the coverage floor — under this criterion refusing to prescribe is a valid prescription, and that null is itself the paper's generation-ceiling result quantified per-mechanism.
proposals.validation: Two-stage, pre-registered. Stage 1 (probes) selects sources and doses; Stage 2 (confirmatory) uses FRESH config seeds never seen in stage 1, and only stage-2 numbers are reported. Stage-2 arms, identical LoRA recipe, paired seeds, 300 eps each on the factorial eval (4 mechanism bands + standard-distribution retention slice + the never-succeed config panel): (1) TFM portfolio; (2) size-matched random/generic; (3) size-matched naive P(fail)-targeted (the incumbent to beat); (4) MISMATCHED-portfolio placebo — same demo types deliberately swapped across mechanisms (approach demos evaluated on tall band, tall-grasp demos on far band, etc.). Arm 4 is the decisive causal control: it holds demo count, source, and generic-fine-tune effect constant and varies ONLY the mechanism pairing. Pre-registered success pattern: (i) tau matrix near-diagonal — matched-band lift exceeds swapped-band lift by >8pp config-clustered; (ii) portfolio beats random on the union of matched bands by >5pp; (iii) never-succeed flips: some configs in treated bands succeed at least once (a high-power binary event given 0.926 deterministic failure-mode repeatability) while random flips ~0; (iv) retention within -2pp; (v) portfolio lift on bands survives on the standard-distribution slice restricted to the same bands (guards the fixed-context comparability break, report §6/§7.3). Falsification patterns, each with a distinct interpretation: mismatched ~ matched => mechanism-matching is an illusion and all lift is generic — the framework is falsified and the honest headline reverts to region-level+coverage (this is the live risk given §13); tau(MimicGen->tall) ~ 0 => the generation ceiling extends past MimicGen, escalate to human/G1 and the ceiling claim strengthens rather than the framework failing; band lift without standard-slice lift => fixed-context overfit, probes are invalid as tau estimators.
proposals.failure_modes: (1) Taxonomy incompleteness: 10.3% config-idiosyncratic variance (instance mesh, yaw, distractors) is as large as all modeled factors; never-succeed configs that classify into no band measure the gap early — if >40% are unclassifiable, run the seed-replay metadata extraction (report §14) before allocating. (2) Fixed-context tau does not generalize to full variation (the §6.3 comparability break): detected in stage 1 itself because every probe arm also carries a standard-distribution slice; band-only lift kills that arm before stage 2. (3) Diagonal illusion via headroom confound — matched bands may lift more simply because they start lower, not because of mechanism match: the mismatched-placebo arm is the specific detector (it evaluates the same low-SR bands under wrong-type demos). (4) Generic-lift contamination if the random control is noisy: mitigated by paired configs and by requiring the diagonal margin (>8pp over swapped), not just margin over random. (5) Dose extrapolation: tau measured at n=120 may not hold at 150+, and new sources may saturate too — run two doses (60/120) for M2 only, the mechanism where escalation decisions hang on it. (6) Retention violation from concentration (verified -9pp failure mode of value/coverage arms): monitored per fine-tune with a kill rule at -3pp on the retention slice; the structural mitigations (coverage floor, interior placement variation, multi-style generation) are in the allocation itself. (7) Stochastic ceiling: ~78% of outcome variance is rollout noise and the config-predictable ceiling is R2~0.22, so even a perfect prescription moves only the deterministic+factor mass — pre-compute the attainable bound (sum of w_m ~ 10-20pp absolute SR) and pre-register it as the expectation, so a +6pp result is read as success against a +15pp bound rather than failure against fantasy. (8) MimicGen inherits its own ceiling (replayed segments may fail exactly where the policy does, e.g. tall grasp securing needs a genuinely different strategy): detected at generation time by MimicGen's own success rate on tall replays — a <20% generation success rate on a band is an early escalate-to-human signal before any GPU is spent on fine-tuning.
proposals.why_beats_pfail_and_influence: Both incumbents were selection rules over a fixed, policy-success-biased pool, and both score the wrong quantity. Naive P(fail) targeting scores WHERE failure is dense but is blind to WHETHER the prescribed data can change it: the arm data is a direct counterexample, since the highest-P(fail) cells were exactly the data-resistant ones — the tall cliff absorbed 610 targeted demos and stayed at 0.14, the rim penalty moved -0.4pp under every arm, and random captured ~80% of the targeted region lift. P(fail) conflates treatable and untreatable failure mass and cannot express "this cell needs a different SOURCE, not more dose". TFM multiplies failure mass by a measured treatment effect per (demo-type, source) — precisely the factor the saturation arm showed can be ~0 while P(fail) is maximal — and its escalation rule turns a measured null into an actionable source switch instead of a bigger wasted budget. Gradient influence fails by the project's own validated principle (influence works iff the loss gradient encodes the target): the causal drivers here are behavioral, mechanism-level properties (a grasp-securing gate at 0.212m, a lateral-reach deficit, perceptual style difficulty) that per-sample action-prediction gradients encode weakly — RC-LESS-v2 landed at 0.590 ~ core even after the whitening fix — and influence additionally inherits the generation ceiling (it can only rank pool demos, and the pool cannot contain what the policy cannot do) plus negative retention (-4.4pp). TFM operates where the verified signal actually lives (dissociated failure mechanisms, additive factor axes), measures transfer directly with cheap LoRA micro-ablations instead of proxying it through gradients, and — decisively — its decision variables (mechanism, demo type, source, dose, context diversity) parameterize the prescription of NEW data, which is the regime the question has moved to and which neither P(fail) ranking nor influence ranking can even represent.

proposals.name: Net Learnability Slope (NLS): axis-additive dSR/dn prescription
proposals.core_criterion: Prescribe data where the NET MARGINAL LEARNABILITY SLOPE is highest: s_jk = dSR_pop/dn_jk — the causal derivative of population success rate with respect to demos added at axis-level j from data-source k — measured NET of the generic fine-tuning lift (the component random data also delivers, which was verified to be ~80% of every prior "targeted" gain). This is the quantity the decision actually needs, and it dissociates the three regimes that raw P(fail) conflates: hard-and-saturated (tall: 610 pool demos moved SR 0.09→0.14, slope ≈ 0.8pp/100 demos ≈ 0), hard-but-learnable (real headroom), and already-solved. Two verified structural facts make the derivative estimable at realistic budgets: (1) factors are additive on log-odds with zero interaction R² (tall×rim, tall×style, rim×style all null with ±5–6pp power), so slopes are probed per AXIS (height band, along-counter-distance band, style tier, category-affordance cluster) — linear, not combinatorial, cost — and cell slopes are predicted by summation; (2) the demo pool is policy-success-biased, so the slope must be indexed by SOURCE (pool replay / GR00T expert loop / MimicGen-from-source-demos / human-G1): zero slope in one source does not imply zero slope in another, and the criterion's output is a full prescription — where, which failure mechanism the demos must exercise, from which source, how many — including the escalation verdict "no sim source has positive slope here → this cell leaves sim" (the generation ceiling, operationalized).
proposals.scoring_rule: Response model with spillover and concave dose: expected population gain of allocation vector n = {n_jk} is V(n) = Σ_i w_i Σ_jk T_ij · s_jk · f(n_jk), where w_i = deployment weight of eval band i (the standard split='pretrain' mix), T = transfer matrix (T_ij = gain at band i per unit on-target gain from demos at level j; off-diagonals are real and verified — tall-targeted demos lifted MID-height objects most, growing the tall-vs-mid gap from −30 to −38pp), and f(n) = log(1+n/n0) with n0 ≈ 100, calibrated to the measured dose-response (0→26.2%, 14→35.1%, 200→37.1%, 610→29.9% stratified-targeted: strong concavity then reversal → also impose a hard per-cell cap n_max ≈ 200 rather than trusting the log forever). The slope itself is a paired difference-in-differences secant: s_jk = [SR_j(base+Δn at (j,k)) − SR_j(base+Δn generic control)] / Δn, evaluated on an identical config/seed list — the subtraction of the matched-budget generic arm is exactly the missing term that let "random capture 80% of the lift" contaminate every prior targeted arm. Decisions never use raw slopes: the allocation quantity is the shrinkage posterior ŝ_jk = B_jk·s_jk + (1−B_jk)·m_a(j), B_jk = τ_a²/(τ_a²+SE_jk²), where m_a is a monotone (isotonic) fit along each ordered axis and τ_a comes from the known true signal SDs (category 0.14, style 0.084 SR). Marginal value per next demo: v_jk(n) = Σ_i w_i T_ij ŝ_jk f′(n_jk); prescribe by descending v (water-filling), subject to the retention constraint in the allocation rule. Demos at level j must exercise that level's verified failure mechanism — approach/reach-rich trajectories for far-along-counter (failures = never-touch, +7.8pp never-touched), grasp-securing for tall (touch-then-fumble, −9.7pp never-touched), instance/visual diversity for style and category-affordance (difficulty-continuum, slower successes) — because s is a property of (cell × demo-content × source), not cell alone.
proposals.estimation: The design problem: a single 300-episode arm has SE ≈ √(0.25/300) = 2.9pp, so an independent two-arm difference has SE ≈ 4.1pp — the 2–4pp effects at stake are invisible naively (exactly why core−random +2.0pp came back ns). Four multiplicative variance levers fix this. (1) PAIRED CONFIGS: every arm evaluated on the identical seed/config list (scene generation is deterministic in seed; seed-replay verified). Pairing removes config-idiosyncratic (10.3%) + measured-factor (11.9%) variance; with between-arm correlation ρ≈0.22 on shared configs, SE_diff = √(2·0.25·(1−ρ)/300) ≈ 3.6pp. (2) MIXED-CONFIG ENRICHMENT: the repeated-config analysis gives an enumerable partition — 28% never-succeed, 16% always-succeed, 55% mixed. All movable probability mass lives in the mixed set, so powering evals ONLY on mixed configs amplifies the observable effect by ~1/0.55 ≈ 1.8× at unchanged SE — equivalent to ~3.3× the episode budget. (Keep a small never-succeed tracking slice for the cell-conversion secondary endpoint; never let it dilute the powering slice.) (3) CUPED adjustment: regress outcomes on the additive factor model's predicted per-config p (R²≈0.12) for a further ~6% SE cut — free. (4) AXIS POOLING + SHRINKAGE: one slope per axis-level pools every eval config in that band; isotonic priors along ordered axes (height, distance) share strength between adjacent bands. Net power arithmetic: a USEFUL slope (~5pp/100 demos population-scale ≈ 9pp on the enriched slice at Δn≈150) gives z ≈ 9/3.6 = 2.5 → ~80% power at one-sided α=0.05 with n=300/arm; the fatal 2pp effects correctly fall below threshold and get shrunk toward the axis model instead of chased (that is the winner's-curse guard: the null best-worst gap at n≈142/id is already 0.19 SR). INFERENCE UNIT IS THE CONFIG, never the episode (verified trap: episode-level permutation p=0.0026 vs correct config-level p≈0.32) — cluster-robust SEs or config-level permutation; each config appears once per arm (within-arm repeats waste budget: design effect 1+(m−1)·ICC, ICC≈0.22). STAGE-1 PROBE (one week, extends the approved 4-arm headroom probe): 6 LoRA arms, all = frozen base(400) + Δn new demos, identical recipe (20k steps, batch 32, fixed training seed; 2k-step smoke gate first): tall×MimicGen (tests whether tall saturation was a pool artifact — MimicGen re-targets source demos and is not policy-limited), far-along-counter×approach-rich demos, mid-difficulty×GR00T-loop (the headroom Middle arm), handled/lidded-category×MimicGen, generic-random-new control (matched Δn, same source mix — MANDATORY, it is the denominator of every slope), base-only anchor. Each arm's 300-ep eval is STRATIFIED across the targeted axis (75 eps × 3 bands + 75 retention random slice), so each fine-tune returns a full ROW of the transfer matrix T, not one number. Cost: generation 4–8h (report actual n collected when rejection sampling fails — that shortfall IS the generation-ceiling measurement), 6×8h LoRA at 2-parallel on the 2×H100, evals ~26s/ep parallelized → ~4–5 days wall.
proposals.allocation: Budget B = 200–600 new demos, two-stage. HARD COVERAGE FLOOR first: ρB with ρ ≈ 1/3 goes to generic/coverage data (random-new demos or pool replay) — grounded directly in the arm results: every arm that fully reallocated lost 4.4–9.4pp on the non-targeted slice, and core's entire real edge was coverage preservation (−0.1pp retention loss); a 2–4pp targeted gain cannot survive a 9pp retention bleed, so retention is a constraint, not a term to trade off. The remaining (1−ρ)B is water-filled on posterior marginal value v_jk = Σ_i w_i T_ij ŝ_jk f′(n_jk): add demos to the current argmax (j,k) until its marginal value falls to the runner-up, repeat; per-cell cap n_max ≈ 200 (the 610-demo reversal); expect the solution to concentrate on 2–3 levels — matching the verified fact that gains are region-level, not cell-level. STOP-LOSS / SOURCE-ESCALATION RULE: if max over sim sources ŝ_jk < s_min ≈ 1.5pp/100 demos (the cost-adjusted indifference point: below this, Δn=150 buys <2.3pp, under the noise floor) for level j, spend NOTHING there in sim and mark j for the next source tier (human teleop → G1 real robot). This makes "which cells leave simulation" an explicit output of the allocation — the generation-ceiling insight as a decision rule rather than a post-hoc story. Retention non-inferiority is enforced at validation: any arm whose retention slice drops >2pp vs the generic control is disqualified regardless of targeted gain. Stage 2 = one confirmatory fine-tune of the full prescribed mix (300–450 targeted + ρB generic) with a mid-dose checkpoint (see failure modes).
proposals.validation: Preregister before stage 2: the allocation vector, endpoints, and margins. Four arms, identical recipe/seed, one shared paired config list: (A) NLS-prescribed mix; (B) matched-budget P(fail)-top-K — the reigning incumbent that must be beaten, not the strawman baseline; (C) matched-budget random-new-data from the same sources — isolates the criterion from the generic lift; (D) base-only anchor. Endpoints: PRIMARY = population-weighted SR on the standard split='pretrain' eval (full comparability with all prior arms; no enrichment games in the headline); SECONDARY = enriched mixed-config slice (the powered comparison, n=300–400/arm, power the single decisive A-vs-C contrast to n≥800 only if the ranking looks right), never-succeed-config conversion rate (the honest cell-level claim: did any of the enumerable 28% flip to mixed?), and retention slice ≥ −2pp vs C. The framework's own decisive internal test: rank-correlation between stage-1 posterior slopes and realized stage-2 per-level gains — the direct measurement of whether a stable learnability derivative EXISTS; the pool-data null it must beat is the verified r=0.06 no-dose-response. Explicit falsifiers: (i) A ≤ C on the primary endpoint → the criterion adds nothing over generic new data; (ii) A ≈ B → saturation-avoidance has no value at this budget; (iii) stage1→stage2 slope correlation ≈ 0 → the derivative is not stable in n and the framework's core object does not exist; (iv) all sim-source slopes ≈ 0 everywhere → the paper is diagnostic-negatives + generation ceiling + G1 (the pre-agreed branch in HEADROOM_PROBE_DESIGN.md). Any of these outcomes is a publishable answer; the design's job is to make them distinguishable at n=300–800.
proposals.failure_modes: (1) Secant ≠ derivative: the slope at Δn=150 may not extrapolate to 450 — the 0→14→200→610 dose curve is non-monotone, so nonstationarity in n is the default expectation, not a tail risk. Detect: stage 2 carries a mid-dose checkpoint (two-dose ladder inside the winning level); if the two doses disagree with the pilot slope, cap allocation at the pilot-validated dose. (2) Enrichment bias: mixed-config gains may not transfer to the population; guard: the headline endpoint is always the standard eval — divergence between enriched and standard endpoints means the enrichment slice is measuring eval-set idiosyncrasy, and the enriched result is demoted to power-only status. (3) Fixed-context transfer failure: slopes measured under pinned (layout,style) may not survive full-variation training/eval (the known comparability break). Detect with one bridge arm trained fixed-context and evaled both ways; if the fixed-context slope collapses under full variation, generate under interior-shrunk variation (placement size (0.15,0.20)) instead of a pinned point. (4) Training-seed noise masquerading as slope: LoRA run-to-run variance is plausibly 2–4pp — the size of the effects at stake. Mitigate: identical training seed/recipe across all arms (pairs the training noise too), and duplicate ONE arm to measure the fine-tune noise floor directly; any slope below that measured floor is declared unrankable by construction. (5) Residual winner's curse: stage-2 realized gains systematically below stage-1 posteriors even after shrinkage; guard: stage-1 numbers are ranking-only, all reported effect sizes come from the preregistered stage-2 arms. (6) Retention slow bleed at unprobed slices: a fixed retention slice can be overfit by repeated selection; redraw the retention sample as a fresh random coverage slice each stage. (7) Spillover mis-estimation: T off-diagonals from 6 arms are noisy, and an inflated off-diagonal shifts budget toward levels that appear to "help everywhere"; guard: floor T at 0, shrink off-diagonals toward 0, re-estimate T from stage-2 stratified evals before any third cycle.
proposals.why_beats_pfail_and_influence: P(fail) ranks cells by the LEVEL of failure; the prescription decision is about the SLOPE, and the verified record shows the two diverge maximally exactly where P(fail) spends its budget: the tall cliff has P(fail)≈0.91 and measured slope ≈0 (610 demos: 0.09→0.14; the saturation arm scored 0.299, BELOW core-200's 0.371), while the actual realized gains came from mid-difficulty cells P(fail) deprioritizes. P(fail) also contains no term for the generic-lift component — random data captured ~80% of its lift and it had no way to know — whereas NLS's DiD-vs-matched-generic-control is precisely that missing subtraction; and P(fail) cannot express source-dependence, while NLS's (cell × source) index is what turns "tall is hopeless" into the testable "tall is saturated IN THE POOL; MimicGen may have nonzero slope; if not, escalate to G1". Gradient influence fails for three now-empirically-proven structural reasons: (a) it scores demos that already EXIST inside a success-biased pool, so it is blind to the generation ceiling — value-influence selecting only 6% targeted demos was the pool literally confessing that the data needed isn't in it; (b) it works only where the loss gradient encodes the target (the validated core principle), and rollout SR is not the training loss — one-step gradient alignment at current θ is a poor surrogate for a 20k-step outcome change (offline AUC anti-correlated with deployed success); (c) it is denominated in loss units with no retention term (−4.4pp retention loss in the influence arm). NLS is denominated in the decision currency itself — pp of SR per demo, measured by actually running the real recipe — includes retention in the same units as a hard constraint, and adds what neither incumbent has and what this lens uniquely supplies: an explicit precision budget (paired configs + mixed-config enrichment + config-level clustering + axis pooling turn a hopeless 4.1pp two-arm SE into ~3.6pp on a ~1.8×-amplified effect, making slope estimation genuinely feasible at n=300) plus shrinkage that makes small-n slopes safely rankable. And its failure mode is itself the result: if every sim-source slope is ≈0, that is the generation-ceiling headline, measured cleanly instead of argued.

proposals.name: Net Attainable Headroom (NAH) prescription
proposals.core_criterion: Prescribe the (region, source, content-type, dose) tuple that maximizes CAUSALLY-MEASURED expected net deployed success gain per unit collection cost. The score is a product of gates — deployment mass of the region x attainability of that region under that source (can the source actually manufacture successful demos there) x marginal teachability of mechanism-matched content at that dose (measured by micro-probe fine-tunes, not predicted from failure rate or gradients) — minus the interference cost of the induced training-mixture shift. Each gate encodes one verified failure of prior criteria: attainability encodes the generation ceiling (pi0 0/14, GR00T 1/9 yield in hard bins — exactly where P(fail) sends the budget); causal region-level teachability encodes the facts that cell-level dose-response is zero (r=0.06), the tall cliff survived 610 demos, and offline proxies anti-correlate with deployed gain; the net-Delta objective with a mixture-shift penalty encodes that retention is the binding constraint (core NT -0.1pp vs value -9.4, coverage -8.9). Regions are defined on the verified ADDITIVE axes (height band, along-counter distance band, style tercile, category-affordance cluster), never on cells, because interactions add exactly zero held-out R2 and per-cell n is hopeless (78% rollout-stochastic variance, config ceiling R2~0.22). Crucially the criterion is a ROUTING rule, not just a ranking: a region unattainable by one source is routed to the next source up the ladder (policy rollout -> MimicGen-from-source-demos -> human teleop/G1), and a region unattainable by every sim source becomes a quantified, budgeted case for real-robot collection — the generation-ceiling claim made operational.
proposals.scoring_rule: Let regions r partition deployment along the additive axes; sources s in {policy-rollout (pi0/GR00T), MimicGen-from-source, human/G1}; content m in {approach/reach, grasp-securing, full-traj, perceptual-variety}; dose k. A prescription is a set pi = {(r, s_r, m_r, k_r)}. Predicted net deployed gain: G(pi) = SUM_r [ w_r * h_r(m_r, k_r) ] - (1 - w_T) * iota(rho(pi)), where w_r = deployment mass of region r (exact from the eval sampler, no rollouts), h_r(m,k) = causal marginal teachability curve for mechanism-matched content (concave, saturating; anchored to the measured dose-response 0->26.2, 14->35.1, 200->37.1, 610->29.9 — knee near k~20, negative marginal past ~200), w_T = total targeted mass, rho(pi) = fraction of the training mixture that is new off-base data, and iota = the empirical interference curve fit from the 7 existing arms (iota~0 at core-like balanced mixtures; 4-9pp at concentrated mixtures). Per-unit score for greedy filling: NAH_r(s,m,k) = [w_r * h_r(m,k) - (1-w_T) * d_iota] / cost(r,s,k), with cost = k * c_s / a_r(s): a_r(s) = per-attempt probability source s yields a usable successful demo in region r; c_s = per-attempt cost (sim rollout ~26s, MimicGen attempt cheaper, human/G1 orders costlier). Content m_r is fixed by the failure-taxonomy mechanism of r, at zero new cost: far-from-sink fails by never-touch (+7.8pp never-touched) -> approach demos with long lateral reach; tall fails by touch-then-fumble (-9.7pp never-touched) -> grasp-securing demos; style/category are a difficulty continuum -> perceptual variety. P(fail) top-K is recovered as the degenerate case a_r=1, h_r proportional to (1-p_r), iota=0 — all three assumptions independently measured false.
proposals.estimation: (1) w_r: analytic from the eval/deployment sampler (category list x placement-band geometry) — free, exact. (2) m_r (mechanism): already computed in the pooled 7,112-episode taxonomy — free. (3) a_r(s): capped-attempt collection probes, ~30 attempts per (region, source), Wilson CIs; before declaring a region unattainable, try the 2-3 known collector configs (min/max_obj_height rejection knobs in record_pi0_demos.py; MimicGen source-demo adaptation); ~half a day for 6 regions x 2 sources; the yield numbers with CIs are reportable results in themselves. (4) h_r(m,k): the expensive input, estimated by MICRO-PROBES: base(400)+K=20 arm-specific demos, 2k-step LoRA smoke recipe, evaluated on the fixed-context instrument (fixed_context.py: pin layout/style/robot-base, shrink placement, vary object) which removes the +/-12pp env noise so per-region deltas are readable at ~90 eps/region. Statistical safeguards, each mandated by a verified pitfall: (a) PAIRED identical config/seed lists for base vs probe — config-level clustering is non-negotiable (episode-level tests are anticonservative: side effect p=0.0026 episode-level vs p~0.32 config-level); paired McNemar/bootstrap at config granularity removes the 10.3% config-idiosyncratic variance from the contrast; (b) Empirical-Bayes shrinkage of h_r toward the family mean before any ranking (the styles analysis already showed naive best-worst gaps are ~0.19 SR under the null — winner's curse is quantified, not hypothetical); (c) disjoint probe/confirm seed batches (probe seeds >=100000, eval seeds <1000, already the convention); (d) a POSITIVE-CONTROL probe first: the pipeline must recover the known targeted-region lift (+9-11pp at K=200) before any novel h_r is trusted — if it cannot, halt (this answers the 'reward inside the noise at n~280' kill-reason); (e) one region run at both 2k and 20k steps early to verify probe-to-recipe transfer. (5) iota(rho): fit once from the seven existing arms' non-targeted deltas — free prior, re-confirmed per validation arm. Total probe overhead: ~4-6 micro fine-tunes (parallelize 2-at-a-time on the 2xH100, ~1.5 days) + ~360 throwaway collection attempts + ~80 probe demos, comfortably inside a 600-demo weekly budget.
proposals.allocation: Greedy marginal allocation on NAH_r(s,m,k) under total budget B (200-600 demos), with four hard constraints. (i) RETENTION CAP: new-data mass rho <= ~15% of the training mixture — the empirical retention frontier (core's balanced regime lost -0.1pp NT; concentrated mixtures lost 4-9pp; K=20 on base-400 is ~5%, safely inside). This is a constraint, not a penalty tune-knob, because retention is the measured binding constraint. (ii) SATURATION CAP: k_r <= knee of h_r (~20 region-level; never past ~200, where the measured marginal is negative) — so the allocator SPREADS small doses across attainable regions rather than dumping budget, the exact opposite of P(fail) top-K, and consistent with zero cell-level dose-response. (iii) ATTAINABILITY GATE with ROUTING: if a_r(s) < ~0.1 (CI excluding 0.3) for source s, route region r up the source ladder instead of dropping it; regions unattainable by all sim sources are logged with their deployment mass w_r as the quantified real-robot/human collection bill — the paper's generation-ceiling deliverable. (iv) AXES NOT CELLS: because additivity is verified (interaction terms add zero held-out R2; log-odds-additive within 1.1pp), a single demo at tall x far credits BOTH the height axis and the distance axis — factorial coverage makes the budget go quadratically further than cell coverage and is a design consequence unique to this measured structure. Content per region is mechanism-fixed (approach vs grasp-securing vs perceptual variety), so 'what kind of demo' is decided by the taxonomy, 'where and from which source' by the gates, and 'how many' by the knee.
proposals.validation: The headline headroom probe directly instantiates the criterion: 4 arms, each base(400) + K=20 new demos, identical LoRA recipe (20k steps, batch 32), identical paired eval seed batch disjoint from training, n~300-400/arm ranking-first, powering only the decisive comparison (NAH vs Random) to n>=800 if the ranking holds. Arms: (A) NAH-PRESCRIBED — the criterion's top tuple: an attainable mid-p region, mechanism-matched content, collected by the routed source (GR00T where it yields; MimicGen for a region GR00T cannot reach — the MimicGen sub-arm doubles as the self-distillation dissociation); (B) P(FAIL)-TOP (hard bin, p 0-0.2) — the FSC-style prescription, with capped attempts and ACTUAL collected-n reported (under-collection is itself a result); (C) RANDOM — the control every arm must beat (random captured ~80% of prior targeted lift, so this bar is honest); (D) EASY (p 0.6-0.7) — saturation/leakage canary. Read three numbers per arm: net Delta (decider), targeted-region Delta, non-targeted retention Delta; plus a mechanism check inside arm A (did the targeted region's never-touch or fumble fraction move in the predicted direction — free from existing taxonomy scripts) and a calibration plot of probe-predicted h vs realized Delta (predicted-vs-realized is a paper figure). FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION TABLE: NAH > Random > Hard ~ Easy ~ 0 => criterion validated, attainable-headroom is the operative signal, proceed to allocation at full budget. Hard >= NAH => core claim FALSIFIED: raw failure targeting suffices, FSC framing wins, publish the negative. All arms <= Random => teachability term undemonstrable in sim at K=20; the attainability term IS the story (measured: no sim source attains the mass that matters) => generation-ceiling + G1 paper, criterion survives as routing only. NAH ~ Hard > Random => attainability irrelevant at this K; retract routing, keep region-level headroom. Easy > Random => leakage/self-distillation artifact; audit config overlap between collected demos and eval before believing anything. All arms retention ~0 is itself a prediction (5% mixture mass under the cap); any arm losing retention at K=20 falsifies the mixture-cap model of interference.
proposals.failure_modes: (1) Probe noise: micro-probe h estimates are the known killer ('reward inside noise at n~280'). Early detection: the mandatory positive control (recover the known +9-11pp effect) before any novel probe is believed; split-half seed stability of the h ranking. (2) 2k-step probe does not transfer to the 20k recipe: detect by running one region at both depths first; if the sign flips, drop the shortcut and probe fewer regions at full depth. (3) Fixed-context ranking fails to transfer to full-variation deployment (the report's own comparability warning): detect by evaluating one arm under both protocols and checking rank agreement; if broken, probes move to full-variation stratified eval and accept fewer, noisier probes. (4) Winner's curse on the chosen region: baked-in mitigation (EB shrinkage + disjoint probe/confirm seeds); detect via the predicted-vs-realized calibration plot — systematic regression to zero means selection is fitting noise. (5) False unattainability: a_r is collector-configuration-dependent; a region can look uncollectable because the rejection knobs were wrong. Mitigation: multi-config attempt protocol with per-config attempt counts reported before any 'unattainable' verdict. (6) Self-distillation confound: h~0 for GR00T-collected content could mean unteachable region OR uninformative source (GR00T shares the weakness). The MimicGen sub-arm dissociates: MimicGen from human source demos is not policy-limited, so MimicGen-h > GR00T-h in the same region pins the ceiling on the source — the cleanest generation-ceiling evidence available. (7) Mass-gaming: a net-Delta objective can drift toward high-w_r easy regions with tiny h; the Easy arm is the built-in control, and per-region Delta decomposition is always reported alongside net. (8) Additivity breaks post-fine-tune (interactions emerge even though the baseline is additive): detect with the existing interaction re-fit scripts on each arm's eval; if tall x distance interactions appear, fall back from axis-crediting to region-level accounting.
proposals.why_beats_pfail_and_influence: P(fail) targeting fails on three independently measured facts, and NAH has one term aimed at each: (i) generation ceiling — the p~0 regions P(fail) ranks first are precisely where no collector yields demos (pi0 0/14, GR00T 1/9) and where the pool cannot contain the fix because it is policy-success-biased; NAH's attainability gate a_r(s) makes this a measured input and converts it from a silent failure into the routing decision (and, when routing exhausts sim, into the quantified case for G1/human data — the anti-FSC headline). (ii) Saturation — 610 targeted demos scored 0.299 < core(200) 0.371 and left the tall cliff at 0.14; P(fail) has no dose model, NAH's concave h_r with a knee cap does, so it spreads budget instead of dumping it. (iii) Retention — the binding constraint that killed value/coverage/whitening is absent from P(fail) entirely; NAH optimizes NET deployed gain with the interference curve fit from those very arms. Gradient influence fails for a deeper, validated reason: influence works iff the loss gradient encodes the target (the three-way-validated core principle), and here it does not — offline AUC anti-correlated with deployed success — and influence can only score data that already exists, so it is structurally blind to the dimension where the verified headroom actually lives: NEW sources, mechanism-matched content, and dose. NAH replaces the gradient proxy with small causal probes — literally measuring the quantity influence tries to approximate (Delta from adding the data) — at a cost of 4-6 micro fine-tunes, cheaper than pool-wide per-example gradients. For the paper: FSC 2505.07728 says 'collect where the policy fails'; the arm results already show failure-rate is where you can neither collect nor teach, and the Hard arm makes that a falsifiable head-to-head prediction inside the headline experiment. The claim 'prescription must be attainability-routed, causally-probed, retention-constrained — and failure rate per se is the wrong signal' is distinguishable from FSC by construction, survivable under every probe outcome (each row of the prediction table is a publishable result), and directly implementable next week with fixed-context generation, K=20 doses, LoRA fine-tunes, and 300-episode paired evals.

judges.best_elements: From TFM: (1) the MISMATCHED-portfolio placebo — same demos, swapped mechanism bands — the only proposed control that causally tests mechanism-matching itself rather than generic-new-data lift (the live risk, since core-random was +2pp ns); (2) the minimal human ask: 1-5 human source demos multiplied by MimicGen, instead of 150-demo teleop arms; (3) pre-registering the attainable bound (sum of w_m ~ 10-20pp given 78% rollout noise) so +6pp reads as success against +15pp possible, not failure against fantasy; (4) retention made structural via diversity inside targeted generation (interior placement variation, >=3 styles) — the mechanism that actually matches the arm evidence (core preserved retention through selection diversity, not base-mix fraction). From NAH: (5) the attainability gate a_r(s) as a measured first-class input — the yields are already measured (pi0 0/14, GR00T 1/9 hard) — with the routing ladder and the 'P(fail) is the degenerate case a=1, h~(1-p), iota=0, all three measured false' framing; (6) the mandatory positive-control probe (recover the known +9-11pp before believing any novel probe) — the direct answer to the documented 'reward inside the noise at n~280' kill; (7) dose caps calibrated to the ACTUAL measured knee (~20). From NLS: (8) the precision budget — paired identical config lists, mixed-config enrichment (power only on the 55% movable configs, ~1.8x effect amplification), CUPED on the factor model, config-clustered inference, and a duplicated arm to measure the LoRA seed-noise floor directly; (9) net-of-matched-generic-control differencing as the definition of the decision quantity. From MHR: (10) alpha_m+beta_s partial pooling across the mechanism-source grid (verified additivity lets ~6 probes inform the whole grid); (11) eliminate/advance on confidence bounds only, with round-2 replication on fresh seeds before any allocation (the cleanest winner's-curse firewall); (12) warm-starting the grid from already-measured nulls (tall-expert, far-expert). Shared and worth keeping: the never-succeed-config flip panel as the high-power binary kill-shot, and frozen-base + identical-recipe discipline.
judges.fatal_flaws: MHR: (a) its return model tau ~ 100-200 demos directly contradicts the dose curve it cites — at 14 demos ~82% of the 200-demo gain is already realized, implying tau ~ 10-20 — so its 150-demo probes and ~300/arm funding levels sit in/beyond the measured saturation zone; (b) round 1 costs ~900 demos including TWO 150-demo human-teleop arms, blowing the 200-600 budget and violating its own escalate-only-after-cheaper-source-fails rule; (c) '50/50 base mix = empirically validated coverage-preserving ratio' is fabricated grounding — core's -0.1pp retention came from selection composition, not any base-mix fraction. NAH: the interference curve iota(rho) 'fit from the 7 existing arms' is mis-specified for the same reason — those arms were all trained on selected sets, yet retention ranged -0.1 to -9.4, so retention is NOT a function of new-data mixture fraction, and the rho<=15% hard cap would forbid regimes like the core(200) mixture that produced the best verified result; it also extrapolates the pool-measured knee (~20) to new sources with no dose satellite, and hangs probe validity on 2k-step-to-20k transfer. NLS: mixed-config enrichment needs never/always/mixed labels that exist only for the 1,178 repeated configs classified under PAST checkpoints (stale, eval-idiosyncrasy risk it only partially guards); stage-1 ~750 demos exceeds budget before stage 2's four matched-budget arms; its mid-difficulty GR00T-loop arm inherits the killed headroom probe's 'no stable learnable-middle' and self-distilling-collector problems; n0~100 in its log dose model has the same knee mis-calibration as MHR (mitigated by the cap). TFM: its pre-registered >8pp diagonal margin is BELOW its own stated MDE (12-15pp at 50 clustered eps/band) — the central claim is underpowered unless pooled across bands. Common to all four: on-demand MimicGen generation is not wired up per the stack scan, and GR00T-generated data carries the documented action-space format landmine — every proposal treats at least one unbuilt pipeline as available; and matched-budget validation controls double or triple true demo cost against the 200-600 budget, which only MHR even partially prices.
judges.synthesis:
Gated Mechanism-Source Race (GMSR). Unit of prescription: (mechanism m, source s, dose k), demo content pinned to m by the verified taxonomy (far→approach, tall→grasp-securing, style/category→perceptual variety). Score = deployment mass w_m (free, from the pooled CSV) × attainability a_m(s) (30-attempt collection probes; pi0 0/14 and GR00T 1/9 hard-bin yields already measured) × net causal transfer τ̂ (probe fine-tune minus matched-budget generic-new control — the subtraction the 80%-generic-lift result mandates). Retention is structural, not scored: 1/3 coverage floor plus diversity requirements inside targeted generation (interior placement, ≥3 styles) — matching the evidence that retention tracks fine-tune-set diversity, not mixture fraction.

Probes: 4–6 arms on the m×s grid, MimicGen-first; human enters only as 1–5 source demos MimicGen multiplies; expert-loop gets one control arm (its tall/far nulls are already measured). Doses near the measured knee (~20–60), one two-dose satellite because the knee is pool-measured. One frozen base, identical LoRA recipe, one shared paired config list; target slices enriched to mixed configs (the 55% where movement is possible), fixed retention slice, config-clustered inference, CUPED on the factor model, one duplicated arm to measure the LoRA seed-noise floor, and a positive control that must recover the known +9–11pp before any novel τ̂ is believed. Estimates are EB-shrunk through an α_m+β_s main-effects model (licensed by verified log-odds additivity); advance/eliminate on confidence bounds only; survivors replicate on fresh seeds before any allocation.

Allocation: water-fill w_m·τ̂/cost at replication-validated doses. Cells unattainable and unteachable in every sim source route up the ladder and are logged with their deployment mass as the quantified G1/human collection bill — the generation ceiling as a decision output, not a story.

Validation, pre-registered: prescribed vs matched-budget random-new vs P(fail)/FSC-style vs frozen base, plus the mismatched placebo (same demos, swapped mechanism bands) as the causal test that mechanism-matching, not generic new data, does the work; never-succeed-config flips as the high-power kill-shot; all effects read against the pre-computed attainable bound (Σw_m ≈ 10–20pp, since 78% of variance is rollout noise). Every outcome row — including all-τ̂≈0 — maps to a publishable claim, and week one needs only the attainability probes, MimicGen wiring, and two probe arms.

judges.best_elements: MHR: (a) successive-elimination discipline — pre-registered UCB95/LCB90 thresholds set BY the measured noise floor (its SE math is exactly right: sqrt(2·p(1−p)·0.78/150)=4.9pp, E[max of 6 noise arms]=6.2pp), round-1 point estimates never reported or allocated on; (b) warm-starting the expert-loop row from already-run arms (tall+expert≈0, far+expert≈0 are measured, not re-probed); (c) the dead-arm≠dead-data diagnostic (training-loss-on-probe-demos distinguishes expressiveness verdicts from optimization failures). TFM: (a) the mismatched-portfolio placebo — swapping demo types across mechanisms holds dose/source/generic-lift constant and varies ONLY the pairing; the single best causal control in any proposal (but must be powered at ≥300 configs/band, not 50); (b) escalation economy: 1-3 human SOURCE demos multiplied by MimicGen, rather than bulk human teleop; (c) MimicGen's own generation success rate on tall replays as a free pre-GPU attainability signal. NLS: (a) the precision stack — paired identical seed lists, config-clustered inference, CUPED on the R²≈0.12 factor model, and above all mixed-config enrichment (powering evals on the 55% movable partition = 1.8× effect amplification ≈ 3.3× episode budget) with the headline always on the standard eval; (b) duplicating one arm to measure the LoRA seed-noise floor and declaring sub-floor slopes 'unrankable by construction'; (c) the matched-budget generic-new-data control as the denominator of every estimate — the exact subtraction whose absence let random capture 80% of prior 'targeted' lifts. NAH: (a) the attainability gate — ~30 capped collection attempts per (region,source) with Wilson CIs, half a day, near-zero cost, and it measures the generation ceiling BEFORE any GPU is spent; (b) the routing ladder making 'this region leaves sim' a budgeted output with its deployment mass as the G1 bill; (c) the falsifiable prediction table where every row is publishable, including 'Hard ≥ NAH → FSC framing wins, publish the negative' — the crispest head-to-head against the key competitor; (d) validation that IS the already-approved 4-arm headroom probe; (e) interference curve fit free from the 7 existing arms. Shared best element (MHR/TFM/NLS): the never-succeed-config flip endpoint — with 0.926 failure-mode repeatability, any flips on the enumerable 28% list is a high-power binary claim immune to the 78% stochastic floor.
judges.fatal_flaws: MHR: (1) Round 1 alone needs 900 probe demos including ~300 human-teleop demos across two arms — at its own 20× cost accounting that is the entire 600-demo budget several times over, and the 3-round campaign plus 4-arm validation is ~4+ weeks, not 'next week'; (2) the α_m+β_s logit-additive decomposition of TREATMENT effects across mechanism×source is presented as 'justified' by the report's additivity finding, but what was verified is additivity of baseline config factors — treatment-effect additivity is an untested assumption doing load-bearing shrinkage work; (3) its pre-registered success (A−B ≥ +5pp, clustered p<0.05, SE 3.5pp) needs a true ~9pp edge over random-new-data when the verified targeted-vs-random gap was +2pp ns — the success pattern is unlikely to trigger even if the method works. TFM: (1) decisive power failure — claimed MDE 12-15pp at 50 clustered eps/band is actually 17.6-20.2pp (verified numerically), and the pre-registered diagonal test (matched exceeds swapped by >8pp) is a difference-of-differences with SE ~10-11pp: the framework's central claim cannot be resolved at its stated sample sizes; (2) stage-1 probes (600 demos) + stage-2 portfolio (600) ≈ 2× the stated budget; (3) seeding fixed-context probe bands with never-succeed configs enriches for the possibly-untreatable set, biasing τ toward zero. NLS: (1) stage 1 needs ~750-900 new demos across 6 arms before any prescription — over budget, and 2 of 6 arms need MimicGen, which the stack scan says is not wired up; (2) the mixed-config enrichment pool is finite (~650 configs) and the partition was defined on past checkpoints — staleness must be re-verified under the frozen base; (3) 'identical training seed pairs the training noise' is an over-claim (different data changes the trajectory) — though the duplicate-arm floor measurement compensates. NAH: (1) h_r ranking at K=20/2k-steps/90-eps has SE ~6pp against between-region h differences of the same magnitude — region ranking is mostly noise, and the positive control (recovering +9-11pp at K=200) validates the pipeline but NOT K=20 sensitivity; (2) the knee-at-k~20 dose model is extrapolated from the POOL dose-response (0/14/200/610) to new sources — quietly assuming pool-derived response shape transfers to exactly the regime where its own generation-ceiling logic says pool evidence doesn't, with no dose satellite to check (MHR has one); (3) the cited pi0 0/14 / GR00T 1/9 yields are not in the verified report and need sourcing. ALL FOUR: every proposal's MDE sits above the only directly measured targeted-vs-random effect size (+2pp ns at ~280 eps/arm), so 'indistinguishable from random-new-data' is the modal outcome — each pre-registers that branch honestly, but reviewers will read the headline as a likely null; and all four depend on MimicGen-from-source generation that is not yet wired up.
judges.synthesis: Adopt NAH's decision skeleton — deployment mass × attainability × measured teachability − interference, with source routing — because attainability is the one gate measurable at near-zero cost (30 capped collection attempts per region×source, Wilson CIs, half a day) and it operationalizes the generation ceiling before any GPU is spent. Replace NAH's unresolvable K=20/90-ep teachability probes with NLS's precision stack: teachability is a net slope vs a matched-budget generic-new-data control, on paired identical seed lists, config-clustered, CUPED-adjusted, powered on the 55% mixed-config slice (1.8× amplification; headline always the standard eval), with one duplicated arm measuring the LoRA seed-noise floor below which slopes are unrankable. Probe at Δn≈150, region level only: at 300 paired configs the honest MDE is ~9pp enriched, so fund at most three probe arms — tall×MimicGen, far×approach-rich, generic-new control — chosen where MHR's warm start already shows the expert-loop row ≈0. Apply MHR's elimination discipline: pre-registered UCB thresholds set by the measured noise floor; round-1 numbers never reported or allocated on. Allocation is retention-first and structural: one-third coverage floor, new-data mass ≤15% of the mixture, per-region caps — but the dose cap is probed, not assumed: one two-dose satellite on the best surviving arm, because the pool's knee cannot be presumed to transfer to new sources. Defer TFM's mismatched-placebo to the confirmatory stage as the single mechanism-matching test, powered at ≥300 configs per band — at 50 eps/band it cannot resolve its own margin. Treatment-effect additivity across mechanism×source is a shrinkage prior to be tested with the interaction re-fit, never a substitute for a probe; only baseline factors were verified additive. Validation is the already-approved 4-arm headroom probe with NAH's full prediction table — including 'Hard ≥ prescribed → FSC wins, publish the negative' — plus the never-succeed-flip endpoint, the highest-power binary claim the 78% stochastic floor permits. Given core−random was +2pp ns, the realistic prior is that the decisive result is a measured double null with one positive exception: attainability probes quantify where sim sources cannot collect, slope probes where they cannot teach, and the paper's claim becomes 'failure rate is where you can neither collect nor teach; prescription must be attainability-routed, causally probed, retention-constrained' — distinguishable from FSC by construction and estimable at n=300–800.
